Phase 2 is alpha-engine-config-I9758; the ruled gate is §6.1's 1 live + 5 replayed (narrowed from 2 live by alpha-engine-config-I10324), NOT §2's superseded "4 consecutive Saturdays". A reader for this row can only be written once a weekly arc has run unattended.

`crucible.keys.verdict_key` gives the real shape, and it is keyed by ARM as well as trading day — so "did one command return a verdict today" is a question about the arm register, not about a single pointer key. The register (`arms/{slot}/register.jsonl`) is written by `experiment.new`, which is still a stub. A reader is writable the day that job lands.

The fleet trial ledger is the real artifact (`crucible.keys.ledger_key`) and it is an append-only JSONL log, not a cost document — it carries per trial rows, not a monthly AWS figure. Nothing in this repository writes a cost reading at all today; `alpha-engine-config-I9828` is where the cost clause's own unmeasurability is tracked, and it must be answered before this row can have a reader.

This objective is enforced by the manifest SCHEMA, which is a repository property rather than a store artifact. The schema passing in CI is not a reading of PRODUCTION, and rendering it MET on the strength of a green test would be the "a merge satisfied the gate" defect this board exists to prevent. A reader would sweep production manifests for a status outside {ok, failed}; that sweep does not exist.

`crucible.alerts` writes one key per INCIDENT per day, deliberately — the weekly ceiling counts incidents, and there is no weekly rollup document to read. A reader must count incident keys across the week's trading days against the declared ceiling; that rollup is not written and counting it here would put the ceiling's definition in two places.

The registry half is a repository property; the explain half needs a real production verdict for `crucible explain` to walk back, and there is none. Rendering half an objective MET is how a partial reading becomes a claim of completeness.

`crucible.keys.arm_register_key` is per-SLOT and is a JSONL register, so "every slot declares both controls" is a read across four registers that `experiment.new` has not written yet — that job is still a stub.
"Flawless from day 1" is proven on the FAILURE path, and the fault harness has not been run against the production store. Nothing about the happy path can substitute for this reading.

`crucible.keys.features_key` is a PARQUET panel keyed by feature version and trading day, not a JSON verdict. Whether R and M read the same version is a question about the two slots' recipes, and the answer belongs in a feature-registry reading that `features/{version}/registry.json` does not yet carry.
